sourcePrinciple.title: Cantillation

sourcePrinciple.paraphrase: The article associates a word’s trope with its stressed syllable, discusses preaccent recitation, and notes possible final-note repetition after penultimate stress. These general statements do not assign all reciting pitches, conditional variants or component-to-syllable boundaries for the inspected tables.

limits: Encoded sign contexts only. Lookup is neither a verified source predicate nor musical word coverage. No word, syllable, phoneme or sound-time allocation is inferred.
Counts and examples are lookup relations, never counts of words with reviewed melodies.
Every reader word and accent is retained; qualified source units, repeated positional signs, maqaf and occurrence boundaries follow the existing source-sign parser.
The same nearby sign context can refer to a neighboring printed column. Opening a figure plays no word and never changes the main musical source.
Printed conditions, source alternatives, unresolved graces/repeats and syllable allocation remain pending; no missing realization is supplied.
No checked modern-sign queries are provided for IdelsohnNo267, which remains a manual chart.
Ordinary Torah source tables are not offered as Haftarah or scroll realizations.
